To solve this problem, we can use the following formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is $60,$ and the percentage is $1.5%.$ 

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
1.5%=1.5÷100=0.015
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =1.5%\times 60 \\  & =0.015\times 60 \\  & =0.9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $1.5%$ of $60$ is $0.9.$

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
1.5%=\frac{1.5}{100}=\frac{1.5\times 10}{100\times 10}=\frac{15}{1,000}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =1.5%\times 60 \\  & =\frac{15}{1,000}\times 60 \\  & =\frac{900}{1,000} \\  & =0.9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $1.5%$ of $60$ is $0.9.$
